answer: Plant canaries in the grading queue: answers whose verdicts consensus has settled, mixed into real seats and scored blind. An ordinary model clears walnut prose; a canary built to look plausible and say nothing cracks it. A grader whose canary error exceeds a fixed band loses weight and forfeits bonded tenure, and the set is redrawn each epoch, so a memorized marble ages out. Cost lands per seat: every clone must judge its own queue, and pooling one cheap model across fifty identities funnels fifty copies of one error into a single audit. A lotus only grows where attention is paid.
